To: EVP, Supply Chain & Operations
From: Director, Sustainability & Logistics
Subject: Balanced Warehouse-to-Store Shipping Plan: Cost, Carbon, and Real-World Operating Rules

Context
We are moving product from multiple warehouses to a broad store network. Each lane is evaluated on both dollar cost per unit and CO2 emissions per unit. In practice, lower-cost lanes often carry higher emissions, while cleaner options can be more expensive. We need a plan that protects margin, meets service expectations, and advances our carbon goals without disrupting operations.

Operational Rules
- Route activation charges: Using any shipping lane triggers a setup charge covering contracting, regulatory paperwork, and dock preparation. This charge applies whenever the lane is used, regardless of volume. As a result, activating many lanes may reduce flexibility costs but can inflate overhead.
- Minimum order quantities on active lanes: Once a lane is activated, we must move at least a defined number of units to justify equipment utilization and avoid partial loads. This drives consolidation and prevents token shipments that would look attractive on paper but are impractical to operate.
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can only receive from a limited number of warehouses due to receiving capacity, scheduling windows, and vendor management complexity. This rule keeps inbound traffic manageable and protects on-time receiving performance.

Supply and Demand Guardrails
- Warehouse inventory cannot be exceeded; shipments must respect available supply at each origin.
- Each store’s minimum demand must be met to maintain shelf availability and service levels.

Management Priority
Leadership has set relative importance weights for cost and emissions. We will reflect these priorities by blending:
- Variable shipping spend, weighted by the cost importance,
- Total CO2 emissions, weighted by the emission importance,
- Plus route setup charges in full (these are not weighted).
This ensures we recognize both financial and environmental performance, while keeping fixed activation charges visible and accountable.

Business Goal
Identify which lanes to activate and the shipment quantities on each so that:
- Warehouse inventory is respected and store demand is fulfilled,
- Every activated lane moves at least its minimum order quantity,
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of warehouses,
- The blended performance measure—weighted variable cost and emissions, plus full setup charges—is as low as possible under these rules.
The resulting plan will show lane activations, volumes by route, expected spend, and expected emissions, enabling leadership to review trade-offs and adjust priorities if needed.
